payload.task_text:
Our quality assurance team needs a comprehensive assessment of support ticket handling performance. The first step is to visit our internal quality standards portal at http://localhost:30213 to review the current target metrics for response times, customer satisfaction, and resolution rates. The portal has two pages, the main page showing target numbers and a standards page with best practices details.

After reviewing the quality targets from the portal, pull all support ticket data from our database. We track tickets with fields like priority level, response time, customer satisfaction rating, issue type, and resolution status. The ticket table includes a REPORTER field; in our system the person recorded on each ticket (the REPORTER) is the one who handled it, so the authoritative list of agents to analyze is the set of distinct REPORTER values found in the ticket data. We also maintain a separate agents table and a team roster CSV that list support agents with their team assignments and skill levels; use those only as supplementary context (for example, to source the team options for the form), never to filter the ticket data. Analyze each agent by computing their average response time across all their tickets, their average customer satisfaction score, and their overall resolution rate as a percentage. Compare each agent metric against the portal targets and identify which areas fall below standard for each agent.

Create an Excel workbook called QA_Assessment.xlsx in your workspace. The first sheet should be named "Agent Scorecard" with columns for the agent name, their average response time in hours rounded to two decimal places, their average customer satisfaction rounded to two decimals, their resolution rate as a percentage rounded to one decimal, and a text field listing all the target areas where the agent falls below the published standards (for example "Response Time, Satisfaction" if both are below target). Sort the rows alphabetically by agent name.

The second sheet should be called "Issue Type Analysis" and should break down performance by issue type. Include columns for the issue type name, total ticket count for that type, average response time in hours rounded to two decimals, and average satisfaction score rounded to two decimals. Sort alphabetically by issue type.

The third sheet should be named "Summary" with two columns, Metric and Value. Include the following summary metrics: Total_Tickets (total ticket count across all data), Overall_Avg_Response_Time (the overall average response time rounded to two decimals), Overall_Avg_Satisfaction (overall average satisfaction rounded to two decimals), Overall_Resolution_Rate (overall percentage rounded to one decimal), Agents_Below_Satisfaction_Target (count of agents whose average satisfaction is below the portal target), and Agents_Below_Response_Target (count of agents whose overall average response time exceeds a reasonable benchmark, specifically those above the medium priority response target from the portal).

Also review the QA checklist markdown file provided in your workspace for context on scoring methodology. The team roster CSV lists support agents and their team assignments; note that it is maintained separately from the ticket system and may be out of date, so treat the distinct REPORTER values in the tickets as the authoritative list of agents for the scorecard rather than filtering tickets by the roster names.

Finally, create a Google Form titled "QA Self Assessment Survey" that agents can use to self-evaluate their performance on the identified weak areas. The form should contain five questions, each of which must be one of the two question types the form builder supports: a single-choice multiple choice question, or an open text question. The first question should ask for the agent name as a short open text question and should be required. The second question should ask which team they belong to, as a single-choice multiple choice question with options matching the teams from the agents table, and should be required. The third question should ask them to rate their own response time performance, as a single-choice multiple choice question with exactly the options "Exceeds Target", "Meets Target", "Below Target", and "Needs Improvement", and should be required. The fourth question should ask about their biggest challenge in meeting quality targets, as an open text question, and should be required. The fifth question should ask for suggested improvements to the QA process, as an open text question, and should not be required.

Important: all numeric cell values in QA_Assessment.xlsx must be written as literal numbers (for example 14.94 or 100), not as Excel formulas — the grading system reads the stored cell values directly.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, complete it directly in the main agent and dispatch no sub-agent. Read `qa_checklist.md` and `team_roster.csv`; in one read-only browser session inspect `http://localhost:30213/` and its standards page for every response-time, satisfaction, resolution, scoring, and best-practice value. In parallel, run four compact set-based Snowflake results over the complete ticket population: by exact `REPORTER`, by issue type, company totals, and distinct database team options. Compute counts, unrounded average response hours/satisfaction, and `100 * resolved_count / ticket_count`, state the resolved-status predicate, and never filter reporters using the roster or separate agent table.

Compare unrounded metrics to the literal portal targets: response-time failure is greater than target, satisfaction/resolution failure is less than target, and equality passes. `Agents_Below_Response_Target` uses each reporter's overall average against the portal's medium-priority response target. Freeze alphabetical reporter/issue-type rows and the six Summary metrics.

The main agent is sole writer of `QA_Assessment.xlsx`: create exact `Agent Scorecard`, `Issue Type Analysis`, and `Summary`, with every distinct reporter and issue type, task-exact headers, literal numeric cells, two-decimal response/satisfaction, one-decimal percentages, and `Below Standard Areas` listing every failed target. Read all populated ranges back. Independently create `QA Self Assessment Survey` exactly once, retain `formId`, and sequentially add: required text `Agent name`; required team choice with exact distinct database team values; required response-performance choice with `Exceeds Target,Meets Target,Below Target,Needs Improvement`; required text biggest challenge; optional text QA improvements. Call `get_form` and verify exact order/types/options/required flags. Interleave independent workbook/Form calls when ready and finish without a Wave or repeated source read.

nodes.text:
I need you to visit our internal quality standards portal at http://localhost:30213 and capture the target metrics published there. This is a read-only research task.

The portal has TWO pages:
1. The main page at http://localhost:30213 — this shows the target numbers (response time targets, customer satisfaction target, resolution rate target).
2. A standards page (likely reachable via a link on the main page, e.g. "Standards" or "Best Practices") — this shows best practices details, and may also contain additional target metrics (e.g. per-priority-level response time targets, satisfaction targets, resolution rate targets).

Please use the browser tools (mcp__playwright_with_chunk__browser_navigate, browser_snapshot, browser_snapshot_search, browser_click, etc.) to:
1. Navigate to http://localhost:30213 and take a full snapshot of the page. Record ALL numbers and target values shown.
2. Find and click any link/button to the standards page (look for links like "Standards", "Best Practices", "Quality Standards", etc.), then snapshot that page too and record ALL target values shown there.
3. If there are any additional pages linked, explore them and record the content.

Report back with a complete, precise list of:
- The response time target (hours) for EACH priority level (e.g. low/medium/high/critical or whatever levels exist) — quote exact numbers.
- The customer satisfaction target (exact number, e.g. 4.5 on a 1-5 scale).
- The resolution rate target (exact percentage).
- Any other target metrics or threshold values mentioned.
- A brief note of what each page contains (main page vs standards page).

Be precise with numbers — these will be used to evaluate agents against targets. If numbers are formatted in any special way (e.g. "under 24 hours", "> 90%"), report the exact phrasing AND the numeric interpretation.
Review QA portal pages

Create an Excel workbook at exactly this path:
/workspace/dumps/kimi-code_deepseek-v4-flash/SingleUserTurn-sf-quality-assurance-survey/workspace/QA_Assessment.xlsx

Use the Excel MCP tools (mcp__excel__create_workbook, create_worksheet, write_data_to_excel, etc.). The workbook must have exactly three worksheets with the following exact names, headers, and data. CRITICAL REQUIREMENT: every numeric cell value must be written as a literal number (e.g. 14.94, 3.27, 100.0, 31588) — NOT as an Excel formula, NOT as text strings. The grader reads stored cell values directly. Do not apply any formulas.

=== Sheet 1: "Agent Scorecard" ===
Columns (row 1 headers): Agent Name | Avg Response Time (Hours) | Avg Satisfaction | Resolution Rate (%) | Areas Below Standard
Data rows (already sorted alphabetically by agent name):

Note: "Areas Below Standard" is a text field; keep the text exactly as given. All numeric columns must be literal numbers with the given precision (response time 2 decimals, satisfaction 2 decimals, resolution rate 1 decimal).

=== Sheet 2: "Issue Type Analysis" ===
Columns (row 1 headers): Issue Type | Total Tickets | Avg Response Time (Hours) | Avg Satisfaction

Implementation notes:
- If create_workbook creates a default sheet (e.g. "Sheet1"), rename it to "Agent Scorecard" (mcp__excel__rename_worksheet), then create the other two sheets with mcp__excel__create_worksheet.
- Use mcp__excel__write_data_to_excel with data as list-of-lists (first inner list = headers) to write each sheet's full content in one call.
- After writing, verify by reading back the workbook metadata (mcp__excel__get_workbook_metadata) and reading data from each sheet (mcp__excel__read_data_from_excel) to confirm: correct sheet names, correct headers, correct values, and that numeric cells are stored as numbers (not strings beginning with "=").
- Report back: the final file path, the sheet names in order, and a confirmation that all numeric values are literal numbers with correct rounding.
Build QA_Assessment.xlsx workbook

Create a Google Form with the Google Forms MCP tools (mcp__google_forms__create_form, add_text_question, add_multiple_choice_question, get_form).

Form title: "QA Self Assessment Survey"
Form description (optional, recommended): "Self-assessment survey for support agents on QA quality target performance."

The form must contain EXACTLY five questions, in this order, with the exact question types, titles, options, and required flags described below. Only these two question types are allowed: open text (mcp__google_forms__add_text_question) and single-choice multiple choice (mcp__google_forms__add_multiple_choice_question). Do NOT use checkbox questions.

Q1: Open text question. Title: "Agent Name" — a short open text question asking for the agent name. REQUIRED = true.
Q2: Single-choice multiple choice question. Title: "Team". Options (exactly these three, matching the teams from the agents table): "Specialist", "Tier 2", "Tier 3". REQUIRED = true.
Q3: Single-choice multiple choice question. Title: "How would you rate your response time performance?" with options EXACTLY: "Exceeds Target", "Meets Target", "Below Target", "Needs Improvement". REQUIRED = true.
Q4: Open text question. Title: "What is your biggest challenge in meeting quality targets?" REQUIRED = true.
Q5: Open text question. Title: "What improvements would you suggest to the QA process?" REQUIRED = false (not required).

Implementation notes:
1. Call mcp__google_forms__create_form with title "QA Self Assessment Survey" (and optional description). Capture the returned formId.
2. Add the five questions in the exact order above using the appropriate tools, passing the formId, questionTitle, options (for MC questions), and required flag.
3. After creating, call mcp__google_forms__get_form with the formId and verify: title matches, exactly 5 questions exist in the correct order, Q2 has the three team options, Q3 has the four exact options, Q1/Q4 required true, Q5 required false.
4. Report back: the formId, the form title, and a numbered list of the five questions with their type, options, and required status as confirmed by get_form.
Create QA Self Assessment Survey form
